name: Jehiel
overview: Jehiel was a male Levite of the Gershonite clan, specifically identified as a second rank Levite and a gatekeeper. He was the son of Ladan, also known as Libni, indicating his lineage within the tribe of Levi. As a Gershonite, Jehiel belonged to the descendants of Gershon, son of Levi, who were assigned particular duties in the service of the sanctuary.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehiel means "G-d [El] lives," reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges the living God. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:18 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant declaration of faith in God's living presence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jehiel as the son of Libni (Ladan) and a descendant of Levi, situating him firmly within the Levitical genealogies. There are inferred paternal relationships to Zetham and Joel, though these are not explicitly stated. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jehiel's role as a second rank Levite and gatekeeper highlights his responsibility in the organization and functioning of temple services, particularly in guarding the sanctuary. His inclusion among the Gershonites underscores the specialized roles assigned to Levi's descendants in worship and temple administration. Jehiel's presence in the genealogical records emphasizes the continuity and order God established for the Levitical service during the time of David's preparations for the temple.
